member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttAssignmentFields`2.Units
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the unit property in the resource assignment collection in the Gantt Chart.
member.value: The name of the resource units property that specifies the resource units of the resource collection in the of the Gantt chart, and referencing .

remarks.para: Use this property to specify the percentage of time or quantity dedicated to a task for a work or resource.

Examples: - Specify 100% if the resource is to work full-time on the assignment. This is the default for all assignments. - Specify 50% if the resource is spending half the available time on this assignment. - Specify 300% if three full-time equivalent resources are working on this assignment. - Specify 250% if two full-time resources and one half-time resource are working on this assignment.
When you want to specify how much of a work resource's time is dedicated to a specific task, or indicate the quantity of material for an assignment, use this property to define assignment units.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttColumn.DisableHtmlEncode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the HTML content of header and content cells should be encoded or not.
member.value: When set to true, HTML content of header and content cells is encoded. Default value is true.

However, if you have already encoded the content yourself, or if you trust the source of the content, you can set this property to false.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttCriticalPathSettings
member.summary: Configures the critical path settings for the Gantt chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttCriticalPathSettings.SlackValue
member.summary: Gets or sets the slack value, in number of days, which is used to determine whether a task is critical in the Gantt chart.
member.value: The number of days between the project's end date and task's end date that must elapse before the task is considered critical. The default value is zero.
member.remarks: Slack is a measure of how many days a task can be delayed without affecting the project's completion. Tasks with zero or negative slack values are critical, while tasks with positive slack values are non-critical. If a task's end date is the same as the project's end date, the slack value is 0, and the task is considered critical. For example, consider a project with an end date of January 15th, 2023. If a task has an end date of January 14th, 2023, and the slack value is zero, then the task is considered non-critical. If the slack value is 1, then the task is considered critical. On the other hand, if the task has an end date of January 16th, 2023, and the slack value is zero, then the task is considered critical. If the slack value is -2, then the task is considered non-critical.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttEvents`1.Filtering
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that is raised before the filtering or clear filtering action is performed in the Gantt Chart.
member.remarks: The event handler receives a object, which contains details about filtering or clearing the filtering action in the Gantt Chart. This event is invoked once with Action argument set to Reset when calling the API without passing the column's field as a parameter. It notifies the clear filtering action, and the event arguments will not be updated in this case. You can prevent the clear filtering action using this event. Conversely, this event is invoked for each field with Action set to Remove when calling the ClearFilteringAsync API with the column's field name as a parameter. In this scenario, you can access detailed information in the corresponding event arguments.
member.value: An event callback function.

member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that is triggered before the Gantt dialog is canceled.
member.remarks: This event is triggered when an attempt is made to close the dialog through any means, including: clicking the close (X) icon, pressing the Escape or Enter key, or clicking the Cancel or Save button. The event handler receives a object which provides details about the dialog's type and allows the close operation to be canceled.
member.value: An event callback function that is invoked before the dialog is closed.

example.code:
<SfGantt> 
                <GanttEvents GanttDialogClosing="OnGanttDialogClosing" TValue="TaskData"></GanttEvents> 
            </SfGantt> 
            @code {

member.summary: Gets or sets the selection mode for the Gantt chart control.
member.value: A value that specifies the selection mode. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property determines how the user can select elements in the Gantt control. When the is set to , the control allows the user to select entire rows of data. When the is set to , the control allows the user to select individual cells. When the is set to , the control allows the user to select both rows and cells.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttSelectionSettings.PersistSelection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Gantt selection should be persisted on all operations. If 'persistSelection' set to true, then the Gantt selection is persisted on all operations.
member.value: true if the Gantt selection should be persisted on all operations; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property determines whether the Gantt control should keep the user's selection even if the user performs other operations on the control, such as sorting or filtering the data. When is set to true, the selection will be maintained even when the control is updated or refreshed. When is set to false, the selection will be lost when the control is updated or refreshed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttSelectionSettings.EnableToggle

member.remarks: When true, the user can toggle the selected row by clicking on it. The toggle action will change the selected row's state, typically visually highlighting or changing the row's appearance in some way. When false, the user cannot perform the toggle action and the selected row remains in its default state.

member.value: Allows selection of only one row or one cell at a time. This is the default selection type.
member.remarks: When the selection type is set to , the user can select only one row or one cell at a time. When the selection type is set to , the user can select multiple rows or cells at a time. The default selection type is .

member.remarks: This property allows you to specify the format of the text displayed in the timeline cells. The format is a string that can include a combination of static text and format placeholders. For example, if the timeline displays hours, the format string "h:mm tt" would display the time in a 12-hour clock format with AM or PM. If this property is set to an empty string, the default format for the timeline unit is used.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.DialogType
member.summary: Defines the type of dialog operation in the Gantt Chart.
member.remarks: This enum is used in the property to indicate whether the dialog is being used for adding a new record or editing an existing one.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.DialogType.Add
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog is being used to add a new record.
member.remarks: When this value is set, the dialog is configured for creating a new entry in the Gantt Chart.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.DialogType.Edit
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog is being used to edit an existing record.
member.remarks: When this value is set, the dialog is populated with the data of an existing entry for modification.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction
member.summary: Defines the method by which a dialog can be closed in the Gantt Chart.
member.remarks: This enum is used in the property to indicate the specific interaction that resulted in the dialog being closed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction.Icon
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog was closed using the close (X) icon.
member.remarks: Selecting this icon typically signifies that the user intends to dismiss the dialog without saving changes.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction.Cancel
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog was closed using the Cancel button.
member.remarks: Pressing the Cancel button generally means the user has decided not to proceed with any actions initiated in the dialog.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction.Escape
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog was closed by pressing the Escape key.
member.remarks: This keyboard shortcut is often used for quickly dismissing dialogs, maintaining user workflow efficiency.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction.Save
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog was closed using the Save button.
member.remarks: The Save button typically signifies that the user wants to save the changes made within the dialog.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.CloseAction.Enter
member.summary: Indicates that the dialog was closed by pressing the Enter key.
member.remarks: Pressing the Enter key often triggers the default action in dialogs, which may include saving changes.

member.remarks: The critical path in a project is indicated by a single task or a series of tasks in a project. The critical path is the longest sequence of activities that must be finished on time to complete the entire project.

member.remarks: Slack is the amount of time that a task can be delayed without affecting the overall completion of the project. It is calculated as the difference of project end date and current task end date.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1
member.summary: Provides information about the TaskbarEditing event.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.Action
member.summary: Gets the taskbar editing action. The available taskbar editing actions are: - ParentDrag - ChildDrag - RightResizing - LeftResizing - ProgressResizing
member.value: Accepts a string value that represents the taskbar editing action.
member.remarks: The Action property represents the taskbar editing action performed in the GanttChart component. It can have different values depending on the type of taskbar manipulation being performed. The available taskbar editing actions are: - ParentDrag: Indicates that the taskbar is being dragged as a parent task. - ChildDrag: Indicates that the taskbar is being dragged as a child task. - RightResizing: Indicates that the right side of the taskbar is being resized. - LeftResizing: Indicates that the left side of the taskbar is being resized. - ProgressResizing: Indicates that the progress portion of the taskbar is being resized. You can use the Action property to determine the type of taskbar editing action that is being performed and respond accordingly in your code.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.Cancel
member.summary: Cancels the taskbar edit action.
member.value: true, if the taskbar edit action can be canceled. Otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.Data
member.summary: Gets the data of the task being edited.
member.value: The data object representing the task being edited.
member.remarks: The Data property represents the data of the task currently being edited in the GanttChart component. It provides access to the data object that represents the task and contains various properties such as task name, start date, end date, duration, and other task-related information. You can use the Data property to retrieve or modify the data of the task being edited and perform any necessary operations or validations on it.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.ValidationMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the data validation mode for predecessor relationships in the component.
member.value: One of the enumeration that specifies the validation mode for predecessor relationships.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.EnablePredecessorValidation
member.summary: Determines whether the task’s date values are validated and updated automatically based on predecessor values.
member.value: true if validation of task date values based on predecessors is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: The EnablePredecessorValidation property controls whether Gantt task dates are validated based on their predecessor tasks. /// When set to true, task date values will be validated based on . When set to false, this validation is disabled. By default, EnablePredecessorValidation is set to true, indicating that validation is enabled.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.TaskbarEditingEventArgs`1.EnablePredecessorOffsetValidation
member.summary: Determines whether to restrict taskbar dragging beyond a predecessor value.
member.value: true if taskbar dragging should be restricted to a date less than the predecessor value; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When EnablePredecessorOffsetValidation is set to true, the gantt chart component will enforce a rule that prevents taskbars from being dragged to a date later than the date of their predecessors. If the taskbar is dragged above the given predecessor offset value, it gets reverted to the minimum predecessor value.

               new GanttAddDialogField(){ Fields = new string[]{"Dependency"}, HeaderText="Predecessor" ,Type = GanttDialogFieldType.Dependency }
             };
             }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.ContextMenuItems
member.summary: Gets or sets both built-in and custom context menu items.
member.value: A list of built-in context menu items names or instance of for custom items.

example.code:
<SfGantt @ref="Gantt" DataSource="@TaskCollection" ContextMenuItems=contextMenuItems EnableContextMenu="true">
                <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress"
                    Dependency="Predecessor" ParentID="ParentId"></GanttTaskFields>
               <GanttEditSettings AllowAdding = "true"></GanttEditSettings>
                <GanttEvents ContextMenuItemClicked = "ContextMenuItemClickedHandler" TValue="TaskData"></GanttEvents>
            </SfGantt>
            @code{
             private SfGantt<TaskData> Gantt;
             private object contextMenuItems = new List<object> { "Add", "TaskInformation", new Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ContextMenuItemModel { Text = "Refresh", Target = ".e-content", Id = "refresh" } };
             private List<TaskData> TaskCollection { get; set; }
             private async Task ContextMenuItemClickedHandler(ContextMenuClickEventArgs<TaskData> args)
             {
               if (args.Item.Id == "refresh")
               {
                  await Gantt.RefreshAsync();
               }
             }
             }

member.remarks:
The available built-in items are,
AutoFitAll Auto fit the size of all columns
AutoFit Auto fit the current column
SortAscending Sort the current column in ascending order
SortDescending Sort the current column in descending order
TaskInformation Displays the current task.
Save Saves the edited Task
Cancel Cancels the edited Task
DeleteTask Deletes the current Task
Add Adds a new row to the Gantt
Convert Convert Current Task to Milestone or vice-versa
Indent Indent the selected record to one level
Outdent Outdent the selected record to one level
DeleteDependency Deletes the current dependency task link.
Context menu items display when clicking mouse right. Enable the built in context menu item using EnableContextMenuItems.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableRowVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable row virtualization on the grid. When enabled, only the rows visible within the viewport are rendered and on vertical scrolling, subsequent rows are loaded.
member.value: true if need to enable row virtualization to render only the rows visible within the viewport, which enhances performance; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If `EnableRowVirtualization` set to true, then the Gantt loads only the rows that are visible within the viewport, which improves performance for large datasets.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableRowVirtualization="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableTimelineVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable timeline virtualization on the chart side. When enabled, only the timeline cells in the current viewport are rendered and subsequent timeline cells are loaded dynamically on horizontal scrolling.
member.value: true If need to enable timeline virtualization to load project with larger timespan with better performance; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If `EnableTimelineVirtualization` set to true, then the Gantt loads only the timeline cells thrice the width of the Gantt element, which improves performance for large time span.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableTimelineVirtualization ="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableColumnVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to enable the column virtualization for the Gantt.
member.value: true if need to enable column virtualization; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If 'EnableColumnVirtualization' is set to true, then the Gantt will Initially, render only the columns that are in the current viewport and also load projects with a large number of columns with better performance. Subsequent columns are loaded on horizontal scrolling. This helps to load a large dataset with a large number of columns in the Gantt.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableColumnVirtualization="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.LoadChildOnDemand
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to load child records on demand in remote data binding. Initially, parent records are rendered in a collapsed state.
member.value: true if only parent records should be rendered during the initial render and child records will be loaded only when expanding a parent record, false if both parent and child records should be loaded during the initial render. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Loading child records on demand can improve the performance of data-bound controls with a large number of records. Child records are only loaded when they are requested, rather than loading all child records at once. This property is not applicable for local data binding.

Search Searches tasks by the given key.
ExpandAll Expands all the task of Gantt.
CollapseAll Collapses all the task of Gantt.
PrevTimeSpan Extends timeline with one unit before the timeline start date
NextTimeSpan Extends timeline with one unit after the timeline finish date.
ZoomIn Zoom-in the timeline
ZoomOut Zoom-out the timeline
ZoomToFit Displays all tasks within the viewable Gantt chart within current view port.
ExcelExport Exports Gantt data in Excel format.
CsvExport Exports Gantt data in CSV format.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.OverscanCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of additional items to be rendered in the DOM before and after the visible items (based on ) when virtual scrolling is enabled in gantt.
member.value: The number of additional items to pre-render before and after the visible items (based on PageSize). The default value is 0.
member.remarks: Adjusting this property can enhance scrolling performance and optimize rendering, especially for large datasets in a virtualized Gantt Chart. By pre-rendering a buffer of extra items that are not yet visible, the component minimizes the need for frequent re-rendering while scrolling. This optimization results in a smoother and more responsive user experience.

member.value: A time zone identifier (for example, "UTC"). If not set, the system's local time zone is used. Default is null.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.AutoUpdatePredecessorOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to validate and update the predecessor offset during task scheduling.
member.value: Set to false to prevent the recalculation of predecessor offsets, thus restricting their validation. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When enabled, the offset is automatically updated whenever task properties including start date, end date, duration, or dependencies are modified. When disabled, the offset value remains unchanged and is taken directly from the data source, allowing for external management or predefined values. In scenarios with multiple dependencies, the highest offset predecessor is prioritized, and other existing offset values are maintained without recalculation.

member.summary: Handles changes to the start date for a task item in the Gantt chart when updated via the StartDate dialog field.
member.param: The new start date value to assign, provided as an object.
The name of the column field being updated, typically indicating the start date field.

member.returns: The updated start date of the task as a nullable object.
member.remarks:
This method validates the provided value for the start date and applies changes to the task item in the TaskItemCollection. It adjusts the ProjectStartDate if the task's start date is earlier than the overall project start. The method also triggers appropriate notify methods to update related fields like the end date and duration based on the condition of these fields.
If the Gantt chart allows for segmentation and the relevant fields are defined, it updates the segments of the task item. Proper validation of the input value is performed via ValidateScheduleFields prior to making these updates.

member.returns: The updated end date of the task as a nullable object.
member.remarks:
This method validates the provided value for the end date and applies changes to the task item in the TaskItemCollection. It updates the task's duration when the duration field is not empty.
If both the start date and the new end date of the task item are specified and valid, it updates the start date picker, ensuring both dates follow a logical sequence.
If the Gantt chart uses segmentation and the relevant fields are defined, it updates the segments of the task item accordingly. Validation of the input value is performed via the ValidateScheduleFields function.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.Internal.DialogValidation`1.ProgressValueChange(System.Object,Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.Internal.GanttTaskItem)

member.param: The new progress value to assign, provided as an object. This value should be convertible to a representing the progress percentage.

member.returns: The updated progress of the task as a double.
member.remarks:
The method updates the progress of a task item within the TaskItemCollection. If the task does not have a duration and unscheduled tasks are not allowed, it calculates the duration for the task. The total progress is calculated as a product of the progress percentage and the total duration in days.
It ensures that the input value is checked for nullability before conversion to avoid exceptions. The task's TotalProgress and TotalDuration are updated accordingly using the parent date module functionalities.

This method updates the baseline start date of a task item from the TaskItemCollection. It performs a validation check to ensure that the baseline start date does not exceed the baseline end date if the system is in an edit state. If validation fails, it throws a indicating the importance of date order for project tracking and analysis.

This method updates the baseline end date of a task item in the TaskItemCollection. It performs a validation check to ensure that the baseline end date is not set before the baseline start date. If the validation fails, it throws a to highlight the importance of having a valid date order for effective project tracking and analysis.
If an exception occurs, such as when the system is in an edit state, it delegates error handling to the ActionFailure method of the parent EditModule. If editing is not enabled, it defaults the end date to the start date.
The method carefully manages the potential nullability of the input value and ensures correct conversion to a .

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.Internal.GanttTimezone`1.GetDateInTimeZone(System.DateTime,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Gets the adjusted date/time value in the configured time zone, including handling of invalid times such as daylight saving time transitions.
member.param: The original value to convert or adjust.
If set to true, performs conversion of the date to the configured time zone. If false, simply validates the provided date for time zone transitions.
member.returns: A value that has been converted and adjusted for the configured time zone, or the input date if no conversion or adjustment was needed.
member.remarks:
This method ensures that the returned date is valid for the local time zone, especially during daylight saving time transitions. It avoids invalid times by finding the next valid time when necessary and performs reverse and standard time zone conversions as required.
Callers should ensure that parent.Timezone and PreviousTimezone are set appropriately.

member.summary: Converts a date from one time zone to another, taking into account the originating, targeting, and system local time zones.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.Internal.GanttTimezone`1.FindNextValidTime(System.DateTime,System.TimeZoneInfo)
member.summary: Finds the next valid that is not an invalid time (such as those skipped due to Daylight Saving Time transitions) in the specified time zone.
member.param: The original value to check.
The representing the time zone to validate against.
member.returns: The next valid value after the input in the given time zone. If the input date is already valid, it may return the same time or the nearest valid time immediately following the invalid interval.
member.remarks: This method uses a binary search approach for efficiency. It is especially useful for resolving times that are invalid due to Daylight Saving Time changes (for example, the hour skipped in spring-forward transitions).
